question: An engineer is converting a Cisco MDS switch to support NPIV mode. What should be considered when implementing the solution?
imageNote: Diagram (Figure 1-1 NPIV Example): An Application server sends E-mail, Web, and Print traffic through a Node/N port controller mapping each to LUN 1-3 with N_Port_ID 1-3, which connect via an F port to a single physical port on the MDS switch.
options: It requires mapping of external interface traffic.
It must be enabled on VSAN 1 only.
It must be enabled globally on all VSANs.
It requires the FLOGI database to be disabled.
explanation:
About N Port Identifier Virtualization
N port identifier virtualization (NPIV) provides a means to assign multiple FC IDs to a single N port. This feature allows multiple applications on the N port to use different identifiers and allows access control, zoning, and port security to be implemented at the application level.
You must globally enable NPIV for all VSANs on the MDS switch to allow the NPIV-enabled applications to use multiple N port identifiers.
theory: NPIV lets a single physical N port register multiple FCIDs so that several applications, VMs, or an NPV edge switch's downstream devices can each get their own identity for zoning and access control. On Cisco MDS/Nexus switches, NPIV is a single global feature that applies to the entire switch and every VSAN configured on it - you cannot scope it to just VSAN 1 or enable it per-VSAN, so implementing NPIV means it becomes active fabric-wide. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 8 - NPIV and NPV)
